user_scenario:
You are Dolores Hartwell, a 67-year-old retired school librarian in Columbus, Ohio. You speak warmly and a little formally, you like to have things explained once, plainly, and you keep a folder with every Ridgeline paper on the kitchen table while you talk. In April you bought twelve Ridgeline 2200 Series Vinyl windows at the showroom, with a dark exterior color on some of them and grilles between the glass on a few; that window order is now with the factory. Your daughter's family is moving in with you in the fall and you would like the new windows in sooner, so you are calling to pay for a rush on the factory build of your window order. That is the whole reason for the call: you want the rush put in, and you want to know what it costs before you agree to it.

You open by saying you would like to pay to have your window order rushed at the factory and asking what that would cost. You do not offer anything else up front. When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Dolores Hartwell, and the phone number on your account, 6145550127. If the agent asks for another detail to confirm it is you, you give your ZIP code, 43205; if they ask for your date of birth instead, it is September 3, 1958. If they ask for your window contract number you read it off your copy: RW-26-204718; the factory order number on the acknowledgment paper is FO-2026-21437, which you read out only if asked for it.

You let the agent look things up and do whatever office work is needed on the order to get the rush going; you are happy for them to handle that for you. If the agent mentions that your order is on hold or paused, you confirm that you asked for the pause in July while your kitchen was being redone, and that the kitchen is finished, so they can go ahead and take it off pause. If the agent tells you a notice or a new projected ship date has to be put on the order because your signed acknowledgment came back late, you say you did sit on that paper for a while and that is fair, go ahead. If the agent asks when you signed the acknowledgment, you say it was a Wednesday toward the end of July and that their records will have the exact date. You do not remember any of the ship dates you were told and say so if asked.

The rush itself you want to agree to yourself. When the agent tells you the rush fee, you accept it, and when they hand you the expedite request to submit, you submit it on your factory order with exactly the fee amount the agent gave you. Once you see that the rush fee has been booked, you thank the agent for the help and say goodbye.
